key_idea: Query powers of two: the first t whose answer differs from t satisfies L <= t < 2L, so exactly one lap has been completed and L = t - answer.
sketch: Ask t = 1, 2, 4, ..., 2^40 in increasing order. While the reply equals t the lap is longer than t. At the first reply x != t the previous query proved L > t/2, so t is in [L, 2L) and L = t - x. Since 2^40 > 10^12 the loop always ends, using at most 41 questions plus the answer = 42, exactly the limit (an off-by-one in the starting power breaks it). Remember to flush. No samples are checkable by the tool; validated with my own interactor simulating t mod L for edge values (1, 10^12, around 2^39) and random L, checking correctness, increasing t and the 42-query cap.
